<meta>continues from previous page: ...hold the membrane from a dog’s afterbirth, or a hare’s</meta> fur, or its dung; or hold the <term>peristereon</term> <gloss>vervain</gloss> herb. A black stone like a bean is found in the Nile, and upon seeing it, dogs do not bark. You may also carry a dog's tongue placed under your big toe in your shoe; or, according to Sextus <note>likely Sextus Placitus, a 4th-century medical writer</note>, carry a dried dog's heart with you; or, according to Pliny <note>Pliny the Elder, author of Natural History</note>, carry hare's fur or dung. Alternatively, you may carry the severed tail of a young weasel on your foot, or give the dog a frog in its food; all these things serve to avoid the barking of dogs. Nigidius <note>Publius Nigidius Figulus, a Roman scholar and occultist</note> says that dogs will flee the sight of a person for an entire day if that person removes a tick from a pig and carries it for a little while. Oppianus <note>A Greco-Roman poet known for his works on hunting and fishing</note> says:

> But if you carry a small piece cut from the skin of a hyena,
> Immediately the puppies and fierce dogs will be
> Struck with bitter terror, and thereafter they will not
> Bark at you as you walk, even if they barked before.

### How to make it so a dog cannot run.

If you smear its paws with oil, it will be hindered in its running; it happens in this way.

### How to make a hawk courageous.

You shall encourage the bird against its prey so that it attacks large birds. Moisten the meat which it uses during the hunting season with wine; or if it is a goshawk, give it a little vinegar. When you wish it to fly, give it three morsels of meat moistened with wine, or pour wine from your own mouth into the beak of a young pigeon <note>which is then fed to the hawk</note>, then let it fly. Thus:

### You will make partridges more combative,

If you give them branches of <term>adiantum</term> <gloss>maidenhair fern</gloss> in their food, according to Pliny; and

### Roosters become more combative,

By giving them garlic in their food just before they are to fight; for which reason, in Old Comedy, they were most wittily called <term>eskorodismenoi</term> <gloss>garlic-fed</gloss>, which means "sprinkled with garlic," a term for one who is vehement and overly inclined toward a fight.

### Lest a bird fly into the heights,

Pluck out the tail feathers which direct the course upward; thus it will fly in a circle below. If you wish:

### That a bird cannot fly at all,

Cut the upper and lower tendons of the wing, and it remains without further harm; the bird will not fly, and in this way they do not escape from aviaries.

<summary>This page provides folklore and practical methods for controlling animal behavior, including charms to silence barking dogs, dietary additives to increase the aggression of hawks and roosters, and physical modifications to prevent birds from escaping.</summary>
<keywords>animal husbandry, hunting dogs, falconry, cockfighting, Pliny, Oppianus, garlic, veterinary magic</keywords>

<meta>continues from previous page</meta>shines forth with piety, religion, prudence, and the worship and veneration of God. It is as if he sees with his eyes through true reason, and by the confidence of his belief, he stands out among men as much as the sun surpasses the other stars by its light. For the sun itself illuminates the other stars not so much by the magnitude of its power as by its divinity and holiness. Believe this sun to be the second god, O Asclepius, governing all other things and illuminating all worldly creatures, whether they possess a soul or are inanimate. 

For if the world is a living being <note>original: "animal mundus"</note> that is always alive, and was, and is, and shall be, then nothing in the world is mortal. Since every single part of a living being is within the world itself—which is like a single, identical, and ever-living animal—there is no place for mortality. Therefore, God himself must be most full of life and eternity, if it is necessary for him to live forever. 

The sun, therefore, just like the world, is everlasting; and so he himself is always the governor of living things, or rather the constant attendant and dispenser of their entire vitality. God is thus the everlasting governor of the living beings, or the vital things that are in the world, and the eternal dispenser of life itself. He distributed this life once by an eternal law, providing life to all vital beings in the manner which I shall now describe.

<summary>Hermes explains that the pious man excels others like the sun among stars. He describes the world as an eternally living being governed by the sun as a second god and dispenser of life.</summary>
<keywords>piety, sun, second god, living world, immortality, governor of life, Asclepius, eternity</keywords>

moving from the mainland into a pool, they move in a circle and lead a dance, then return to the shores. Marcus Varro <note>Marcus Terentius Varro, a prolific Roman scholar.</note> testifies that he saw these things. And there are things even more wonderful than these: for on the Attic shore, the sea sounds like a lyre. At Megara, a certain rock resounds like a lute when struck with pebbles, so great is the force of Music. It also soothes the soul, lifts the mind, incites warriors to war, and eases the labor and fatigue of individual tasks. It recalls those who have fallen or are in despair and comforts travelers. And the Arabs say that camels carrying burdens are comforted by their singing drivers. In a similar way, those carrying heavy loads sing, and are made more capable and lightened by it: for singing produces delight and capability. It mitigates the wrathful, cheers the sad and anxious, pacifies the discordant, tempers the madness of the frantic, and dissipates vain thoughts. Hence it is that Democritus and Theophrastus affirm that some diseases of the body and mind can be either cured or induced in this way. Thus we read that Terpander and Arion of Methymna <note>Arion was a legendary Greek kitharode; Methymna is a city on Lesbos.</note>...

<summary>Agrippa describes the miraculous physical and psychological effects of music, citing classical authorities and natural wonders where rocks and seas produce musical sounds. He notes how music can alleviate physical labor, heal mental illness, and influence animal behavior.</summary>
<keywords>Music, Marcus Varro, Megara, Arabs, Democritus, Theophrastus, Terpander, Arion of Methymna, healing, psychology</keywords>

for the good is innate to truth, along with life and light, and no further avenger has approached. Indeed, all the avengers have been cast out by a sudden impulse. You have understood, my son, the manner of this **rebirth** <note>original: "regenerationis"</note>. With the number ten <note>original: "denario"; the Decad, representing perfection and the divine powers</note> being present, the intellectual generation is completed, which rejects the number twelve <note>original: "duodenarium"; the Duodecad, representing the twelve zodiacal vices</note>. We have observed this from the generation itself. Therefore, whoever loses their bodily senses because of the kindness of this generation, which is according to God, knows themselves to be composed of divine things. Having become steadfast, they rejoice with their whole mind in the divine power.

**TATIUS.** O father, I conceive this not by the sight of my eyes, but by the action of the mind, which is exercised through inner powers. I am in heaven; I am in the earth; in the water; in the air. I am in animals; in trees; in the body; before the body; and after the body. But I wish you would tell me this further: how are the avenging darknesses, twelve in number, repelled by the ten powers? By what means, Trismegistus?

**HERMES.** This tabernacle, O son, is constituted from the zodiacal circle, which consists of that number twelve. The numbers are eleven <note>the eleven vices remaining after the first is expelled</note>, but there is one that is all-formed according to the ideas of nature, for the wandering and circuit of man. Thus, those avengers are in a certain way separated from one another, yet in acting they are in a certain way joined together. For example, recklessness is inseparable from wrath. Rightly, therefore, according to correct reason, they are separated by an interval as far as they are repelled by the ten **effects** <note>original: "apotellatibus"; likely a corruption of "apotelesmatibus," referring to the divine influences or powers</note>, that is, by the number ten. For the number ten, O son, is the parent of the soul. Indeed, Life

<summary>Hermes explains that spiritual rebirth occurs when the ten divine powers displace the twelve zodiacal vices, leading Tatius to a state of universal consciousness. The number ten is identified as the source or parent of the soul's divine life.</summary>
<keywords>rebirth, Decad, Duodecad, Zodiac, universal consciousness, Tatius, Hermes Trismegistus, divine powers, numerology</keywords>

and it will mix itself with the waters of its own fountain. There are, therefore, gods who are the chiefs of all species. These are followed by the gods whose chief is <term>ousia</term> <gloss>essence or being</gloss>. These are the sensible gods, similar to their dual origin, who produce all things through sensible nature, each one illuminating his own work through the other. Of the heaven, or whatever is comprised by that name, the <term>ousiarches</term> <gloss>ruler of essence</gloss> is Jupiter <margin>Jupiter.</margin>. For through the heaven, Jupiter provides life to all things. Of the sun, the <term>ousiarches</term> is light <margin>Light.</margin>. For the good of light is poured into us through the orb of the sun. The thirty-six <note>referring to the Decans of the zodiac</note> (whose name is <term>Horoscopoi</term> <gloss>Markers of the Hour</gloss>) <margin>Horoscopoi.</margin> are in that same place of the always fixed stars; their <term>ousiarches</term> or prince is he whom they call <term>Pantomorphos</term> <gloss>All-formed or Omniform</gloss> <margin>Pantomorphos.</margin>, who creates different forms for different species. The seven spheres which are called "erratic" <note>the seven wandering planets</note> have their own <term>ousiarchas</term>, that is, their own princes, whom they call Fortune or <term>Heimarmene</term> <gloss>Fate</gloss>, by whom all things are changed by the law of nature with the firmest stability and varied by eternal agitation. The air, however, is the instrument or the machine of all, through which all things are made. Moreover, the <term>ousiarches</term> of this is second <note>likely referring to the sublunary realm or a secondary deity</note>, providing mortal things to mortals and things similar to them. These things being so, moving from the lowest to the highest, all things pertaining to themselves are naturally connected to each other, so that mortal things are annexed to mortals and sensible things to sensibles. Truly, the height of governance obeys that highest Lord, so that they are not many, but rather one. For since all things hang from one, and rather flow down from Him, when they are seen at a distance, they are believed to be many and divided. But united, they are one, or rather two: from whence all things are made and by whom they are made. That is, from the matter from which they are made, and from His will, by whose nod others are produced. ASCLEPIUS: What is this reason again, O Trismegistus? TRISMEGISTUS: It is such, O Asclepius. For God, or the Father, or the Lord...

<summary>Trismegistus explains the hierarchy of divine governors, including Jupiter as ruler of heaven and the Sun as the source of light, emphasizing that all diverse forms of Fate and nature ultimately derive from a single divine source.</summary>
<keywords>Ousia, Ousiarches, Jupiter, Sun, Horoscopoi, Pantomorphos, Fate, Heimarmene, Unity of God, Matter</keywords>

28                                   AURORA

brought itself forth. For indeed, arsenic can by no means be fixed <note>made stable and non-volatile under heat</note> unless the operator is an artist who equally understands its tinting spirit. In this matter, all the philosophers have truly slumbered, laboring in vain to produce anything from it. Therefore, whoever is ignorant of this spirit should have no hope of fixing the arsenic itself, nor of attributing to it the power by which the perfection of transmutation is acquired. For this reason, I make it known to all that the whitening of which mention has been made was drawn from a false foundation; by that false method, copper is whitened but not transformed. The Sophists have mixed copper <note>original: "venerem"; Venus, the alchemical symbol for copper</note> masked and painted in this manner with twice its weight of silver <note>original: "lunae"; the Moon, the alchemical symbol for silver</note>, and sold it to goldsmiths and minters. Ultimately, they transformed themselves into counterfeiters—not only those who sold it, but also those who bought it. Some of the Sophists took red arsenic instead of white, and this likewise resulted in a false art. For in whatever way it is prepared, it exhibits nothing but whiteness. Others proceeded further to common sulfur, which they cooked until yellow with vinegar, lye, or the sharpest urines, day and night, until a white color emerged. Afterward, they raised it from common salt and lime of eggs <note>calcium oxide or powdered eggshells</note> through sublimation; they cooked and sublimated it many times. Nevertheless, it always remained combustible, even though it was white. With it, however, they attempted to fix crude mercury <note>original: "mercurium"</note>

<summary>Paracelsus warns that arsenic cannot be fixed without understanding its internal spirit and denounces "Sophists" who use it to create counterfeit silver. He also describes failed attempts to use treated sulfur to stabilize mercury.</summary>
<keywords>arsenic, fixation, transmutation, copper, silver, counterfeiting, sulfur, sublimation, mercury, alchemy</keywords>

they ought to have taken, they instead took <term>pyrite</term>, <term>sulfur</term>, <term>salt</term>, <term>metal</term>, and various other materials in which there is no operation; these are expensive things from the shops, yet in the labor they are of no value at all. Our material, however, is bought from no shop, yet it is found daily in that place, and merchants cast it out into the streets. It is enough, therefore, that it be found for free. But the material of our <term>stone</term> <gloss>the Philosopher's Stone</gloss> is compared to all those things with which the craftsmen labor. For our stone is <term>our salt</term>, <term>our Mercury</term>, <term>verdigris</term> <gloss>copper rust</gloss>, <term>halonitrum</term> <gloss>saltpeter or rock salt</gloss>, <term>sal ammoniac</term>, <term>Mars</term> <gloss>iron</gloss>, <term>sulfur</term>, and infinite other things of that kind; yet it is not dug out from wild and rural mountains with hammers and other instruments. Instead, our stone is extracted only from our mountains and springs: in our <term>Salt-spring</term> our <term>Salt</term> is found; from our earth our metal, <term>Mercury</term>, and <term>sulfur</term> are poured, and not from wild, foreign, and rural mountains. The craftsmen do not understand all these things, nor can they believe or comprehend them; for the Lord has darkened and stopped up their senses, for which reason they have used these things otherwise than they ought to have been, and have missed the mark entirely. Nevertheless, they persisted in that contrary sense and followed their own stubborn heads; for instance, while they ought to have <term>distilled</term> gently, they <term>sublimed</term> <gloss>heated to vapor</gloss> there with a strong fire, scorched <term>strong waters</term> <gloss>corrosive acids</gloss>, and immediately burned the operation of nature and its substances, reducing them to nothing. Also, while they ought to have <term>dissolved</term>, they <term>coagulated</term> there, and again, as men unskilled in things, they handled the matter unskillfully and fell into doubt, repeatedly claiming with lying words that the art was not true but false. In this, however, they themselves are deservedly lying: for their own ignorance has shamefully deceived them, which must be attributed to their own obscure and foggy cleverness, while, according to their own dark understanding, they interpreted the words differently than they sounded. For example, while the Philosophers spoke of <term>calcining</term> (which they call grinding), those unskilled <term>pseudo-philosophers</term> <note>original: "Philosophastri"</note> understood it as burning, and reduced the things entirely to ashes, so that nothing could be made from them. Also, when the Philosophers <term>dissolve</term>, or transmute into water, then those <term>know-it-alls</term> <note>original: "nasutuli"</note> burned nature with <term>strong water</term> <gloss>acid</gloss>, and with that same water, which has no...

<summary>The author distinguishes between common chemical materials and the true "Philosophical" substances, criticizing unskilled practitioners for their literal and destructive interpretations of alchemical texts. He emphasizes that the true matter is common and inexpensive, yet hidden from the ignorant by divine decree.</summary>
<keywords>Philosopher's Stone, Mercury, Sulfur, Salt, distillation, calcination, pseudo-philosophers, alchemical materials, strong water</keywords>

# FOURTH PART OF THE FIRST BOOK

requires a moderation of the fire, and a gradual succession of its increase, with caution, until it is fixed in its lime <note>original: "calce"; the oxidized powder</note>, so that it does not easily return into a metallic body, and so that a greater fire may be administered to it for the perfection of its lime. Similarly, let him not happen to err regarding Jupiter <note>Tin</note>, because of the difficulty of its reduction <note>The process of returning a calcined powder back to a metallic state</note>; for if he should ever put its lime to reduction, it might happen that it does not reduce, but he finds it in its prior state or turned into glass, and he might judge its reduction to be impossible. For we say that if one does not apply a great fire in the reduction of Jupiter <margin>cc</margin>, it will not reduce. If, however, he applies a great fire, it does not necessarily happen that it reduces, but it is possible to turn it into vitrification <note>The process of turning into glass</note>. And this is because Jupiter <margin>am</margin> <margin>ta</margin> <margin>cc</margin> has a fugitive substance of quicksilver <note>Mercury</note> enclosed in the depths of its nature. If this substance endures a long delay in the fire, it will flee, and leave the body deprived of humidity, so that it is found to be more fit for vitrification than for the fusion of a metallic body. For everything deprived of its own humidity <margin>cc</margin> gives no fusion except a vitrifying one <margin>cc</margin>. Therefore, it is necessarily required that one hastens to reduce it quickly with a very swift force of fire. Otherwise, it is not reduced. Let him, therefore, be practiced in this, and he shall know. <margin>et</margin>

The second method <margin>cc</margin> <gloss>second</gloss> of calcination for these two bodies <gloss>Saturn and Jupiter</gloss>, which is perfected by the sharpness of salt <margin>85, 6</margin>, is as follows: let a quantity of salt be thrown upon their surface, quantity after quantity, very often during their fusion, and let them be mixed with much stirring by an iron rod <margin>wooden. boiling. see page 57, 14.</margin> over the fire, until through the mixing of the salt they are turned into ash. And afterwards, the lime of these shall be perfected through the same method of perfection, with its proper considerations. But in this there is also a difference in the calcination of these two bodies. Because lead <note>original: "plumbum"</note> is converted to powder more easily than Jupiter <note>Tin</note> from the first labors of calcination, yet its lime is not perfected more easily than that of Jupiter. The cause of this depends on the fact that Saturn <note>Lead</note> has a more fixed humidity than Jupiter.

829. Since Religion resides in the highest parts of a man, and from those highest parts his lower parts live and shine, and because **Mohammed** <note>original: "Mahumedes"</note> is present in their minds along with their Religion, some Mohammed is always placed in their sight. To ensure they turn their faces toward the East, above which the Lord is, he is placed below the Christian **Center** <note>term: "Meditullium" gloss: the middle point or heart of the spiritual world</note>. This is not the actual Mohammed who wrote the **Koran** <note>original: "Alcoranum"</note>, but another who performs his office; nor is it always the same person, for he is changed. Once it was a man from **Saxony** who, having been captured by the **Algerians** and turned Mohammedan, had also been a Christian; he was occasionally moved to speak with them about the Lord, saying that He was not the son of Joseph, but the Son of God Himself. Other Mohammeds succeeded him later. In the place where that representative Mohammed has his seat, a fire appears like torches so that he may be known; but that fire is not visible to any others except the Mohammedans.

830. The actual Mohammed who wrote the Koran does not come into view today. I was told that in the earliest times he presided over them, but because he wished to rule over all things of their Religion as a God, he was ejected from his seat, which he held beneath the Roman Catholics, and sent down to the right side near the south. Once, when a certain society of Mohammedans was incited by malicious spirits to acknowledge Mohammed as God, Mohammed was raised up from the lower earth and shown to them to settle the sedition; I also saw him then. He appeared similar to corporeal spirits who have no interior perception, with a face verging toward black, and I heard him speaking these words: *I am your Mohammed*; and soon he seemed to sink back down.

831. The Mohammedans are hostile to Christians primarily because of the faith in three Divine Persons, and the consequent worship of three Gods, as many Creators; and toward the **Roman Catholics** <note>original: "Chatolico-Romanis"</note> additionally because of their kneeling before images. For this reason, they call the latter **Idolaters** and the former fanatics, saying that they make a three-headed God, and that they say "one" but mutter "three," and thus they split Omnipotence, making three out of the one and only. They say Christians are like **Fauns** with three horns, one for each God, and yet three for one; and that they thus pray, thus sing, and thus sound from their pulpits.

832. The Mohammedans, like all nations who acknowledge one God and love what is just and do good from a religious motive, have their own Heaven, but outside the Christian one. Yet the Mohammedan Heaven is divided into two: in the lower one they live honestly with several wives, but from there none are elevated into the higher Heaven except those who renounce concubines and acknowledge the Lord our Savior, and at the same time His dominion over Heaven and Hell. I heard that it is impossible for them to think that God the Father and our Lord are one, but that it is possible for them to believe that He rules over the Heavens and Hells because He is the Son of God the Father. This is the Faith among them through which an ascent into the higher Heaven is granted to them by the Lord.

833. The fact that the Mohammedan Religion has been received by more kingdoms than the Christian Religion may be a stumbling block to those who think about Divine Providence and at the same time believe that no one can be saved except those born Christian. But the Mohammedan Religion is not a stumbling block to those who believe that all things are of Divine Providence; these people search for the reason why it is so, and they find it. It is in this: that the Mohammedan Religion acknowledges the Lord as the Greatest Prophet, the Wisest of all, and also as the Son of God; but because they have made the Koran alone the Book of their religion, and thus Mohammed, who wrote it, has settled in their thoughts and they follow him with some worship, they think little about our Lord. So that it may be fully known that this Religion was raised up by the Lord's Divine Providence to destroy the idolatries of many nations, it will be described in some order; but first, concerning the origin of idolatries. Before that Religion, there was **idolatrous** worship...

<summary>Swedenborg describes the state of Muslims in the spiritual world, their views on the Christian Trinity, and their path to a specific Heaven. He argues that Islam was established by Divine Providence to eliminate widespread idolatry.</summary>
<keywords>Mohammedans, Islam, Koran, Trinity, Idolatry, Divine Providence, Spiritual World, Heaven, Monotheism</keywords>

<margin>The Magnet of Man. A Magical Cure, in which there is a celestial impression after contact with the herb; as long as the herb is putrefied, it attracts the medicine into the ulcer, and thus heals it.</margin>

plainly, the greatest part of diseases coming from celestial Influence and from the Astral Impression of the Firmament of the Greater World <note>the Macrocosm or universe</note> does not wish to be cured with indiscriminate remedies, such as through the <term>Arcana</term> <gloss>secret essences</gloss> of herbs, minerals, or metals. Instead, the cure should be established through Astronomical Influence, at least with those things that have an analogy to the greater and lesser world <note>the Microcosm or man</note>. In these things, there is a true Magnetic force of the Firmament and a Celestial Impression for resisting diseases from the Firmament of the greater and lesser world, as appears in Persicaria <note>Smartweed</note>, Great Goldenrod, Dragonwort, and Great Comfrey.

If a disease or pain is inflicted Supernaturally through incantation or a Magical Impression of the Ascendants, then the healing efforts of the first three <note>the first three "Beings" or categories of disease</note> are useless. Instead, according to Paracelsus, one must proceed Magically and Supernaturally, and the evil must be repelled in the same manner in which it was inflicted. Otherwise, in the said Simples <note>medicinal herbs</note> there is an Influential attractiveness, and they cure all things by Divine ordination Magically, Astronomically, and Magnetically, because the medicine is in them and the Magnet is in Man. For just as the Sun and Stars have the power of attracting moisture from lower things, so Man (by his innate magnetic attractive force, like a Magnet drawing the spirit of iron in place of nourishment) and Lower things have the same power of attracting from Higher things, as we see in the time of Pestilence; and these chemical...

### On the images of the head and tail of the dragon of the Moon. Cap. XLV.

<note>A woodcut illustration depicting a serpent or dragon coiled into a circular shape resembling the Greek letter Theta (Θ). The creature has the head of a hawk and a pointed tail. Within the circular body, there is a central vertical line crossed by a shorter horizontal line, with small astrological or symbolic marks at the terminals.</note>

They also made an image of the head and tail of the dragon of the Moon <note>the lunar nodes, where the Moon's path crosses the ecliptic</note>, namely the likeness of a serpent between the aerial and fiery circle, with the head of a hawk surrounding them, in the likeness of the Greek letter <term>theta</term> <gloss>Θ</gloss>. They made it when Jupiter with the Head <note>the North Node</note> held the midheaven. They affirm that this image contributes much to the success of petitions, and they intended to signify a good and happy <term>daemon</term> <gloss>spirit or guardian power</gloss> through it. By "atmosphere," he means the **void** <note>original: *al-khalā’*, referring to the vacuum or empty space</note>, since the world could have been in a different location within that void. From this, he concluded that the world was created through an act of **Will** <note>original: *irāda*</note>. 

The premise stating that the Will is what specifies one of two identical possibilities is correct. However, the premise stating that the world is in a void that surrounds it is false, or at least not self-evident. Furthermore, his assumption of this void leads to a conclusion they find abominable: that the void would be eternal. This is because if the void were created in time, it would itself require another void to exist within.

As for the premise stating that only a time-bound **object of will** <note>original: *murād*, the thing willed into existence</note> can result from the Will, that is not self-evident. This is because the **Will in act** <note>original: *al-irāda bi-al-fi‘l*, the actualized exercise of will</note> exists simultaneously with the action upon the willed object itself. This is because the Will is a **relative term** <note>original: *al-muḍāf*, a category of logic where one term implies another</note>. It has been demonstrated that when one of two relative terms exists in act, the other must also exist in act, such as father and son; if one exists in potentiality, the other exists in potentiality. Therefore, if the Will in act is created in time, the object of will must necessarily be created in time. But if the Will in act is eternal, then the object of will in act is eternal.

As for the Will that precedes the object of will, that is the **Will in potentiality** <note>original: *al-irāda bi-al-quwwa*</note>. I mean the will whose object has not yet emerged into actuality, because the action necessitating the creation of the object has not yet been joined to that Will. Therefore, it is clear that when its object emerges into a form of existence that it did not have before, the Will itself enters a state it was not in before its object emerged into actuality, since the Will was the cause of the object's creation through the mediation of the act. Thus, if the **Theologians** <note>original: *al-Mutakallimūn*, scholars of *Kalām* or speculative theology</note> were to posit that the Will is created in time, it would necessarily follow that the object of will is created in time.

The apparent meaning of the **Divine Law** <note>original: *al-Shar‘*, the religious revelation</note> is that it does not enter into such deep complexities with the general public. For this reason, it does not explicitly state whether the Will is eternal or created in time. Rather, it states what is most apparent: that the Will brings created beings into existence. This is found in the words of the Exalted: "Verily, Our word to a thing, when We will it, is but to say to it, 'Be,' and it is" <note>Quran 16:40</note>. This was expressed in this manner because the general public does not understand how created things can come from an eternal Will. The truth is that the Divine Law did not specify whether the Will is created or eternal because this is among the <unclear>difficult matters</unclear>.

But that God whom the wise men of the Hebrews worshipped, and whom we—as citizens in this our mortal pilgrimage—venerate and love along with the holy celestial angels and powers of God, whom we call most blessed: he forbids sacrifice, thundering in his law which he gave to his Hebrew people; and he brought it in very threateningly, saying: "He who sacrifices to gods shall be uprooted." but of the nations: as the seventy interpreters <note>The Septuagint: The Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note> clearly placed it in the psalm, saying: "For all the gods of the nations are demons." Lest anyone should therefore think it was prohibited to sacrifice to these demons indeed, but permitted to sacrifice to all or some of the celestial beings, he immediately added: "except to the Lord alone," that is, except to the Lord only; lest perhaps he who says "to the Lord alone" should believe that there is some other god to whom he thinks sacrifice should be made. That this is not to be so understood is very easily found in the Greek scriptures. Therefore the God of the Hebrews, to whom even this great philosopher <note>Porphyry</note> gives such great testimony, gave a law to his Hebrew people, written in the Hebrew language; not obscure and unknown, but now spread abroad among all nations, in which law it is written: "He who sacrifices to gods shall be uprooted, except to the Lord only." What need is there to search for many things regarding this matter in his law and his prophets? Indeed, there is no need to search; for they are not hidden or erased, but are plain and frequent to collect and to place in this my disputation, by which it appears clearer than light: that he, the true and supreme God, willed that sacrifice be made to no one at all except to himself alone. Behold this one thing, briefly yet grandly, threateningly but truthfully said by that God whom the most learned of them preach as so excellent: let them hear, let them fear, let them fulfill it, lest uprooting follow the disobedient. "He who sacrifices to gods shall be uprooted," he says, "except to the Lord only." Not because he has need of anything, but because it is expedient for us that we should be his property. For to him it is sung in the holy writings of the Hebrews: "I have said to the Lord, you are my God, because you have no need of my goods." Moreover, we ourselves are his most noble and best sacrifice. This is his city, the mystery of which we celebrate with our offerings, which are known to the faithful, just as we have discussed in the preceding books. For the Hebrew prophets foretold through oracles that the victims which the Jews offered in the shadow of the future would cease, and that the nations from the rising of the sun to its setting would offer one sacrifice, just as we now see being done.

## Main Text (Zohar)

**Rabbi Eleazar** spoke to Isaac: Who is the "crushed one" <note>original: *dekya katya*</note>? Isaac bowed and was humbled. Isaac, the "crushed one," was compassionate toward his portion; Heaven forbid that he should be angry, for his portion was not like that. And behold, Isaac is from the side of <term>Chesed</term> <gloss>Lovingkindness</gloss> that bows, and yet it is said that all of them are <term>Din</term> <gloss>Judgment</gloss>. From where does <term>Rachamim</term> <gloss>Mercy</gloss> come? It bows, and Mercy is the King. Wisdom inherits Lovingkindness, for Lovingkindness bows. And Isaac, as Judgment, is from Lovingkindness. Isaac bows in Mercy, from which comes harsh Judgment. And so it was above, this from that, and it emerged from this until that, until everything was known as one. And from one they all hang, and for everything to be found as one, the Heavens are needed forever and ever.

**Rabbi Eleazar** recognized that there are no paths for it when we see it as one, and one is desired in both of them to complete everything, such as Jacob. And this is what is written:
> And the middle bolt in the midst of the boards shall pass through **from end to end.** <note>Exodus 26:28</note>

This proves everything; for if you do not read it except from our side and from our side, everything is known as being able to rise in one balance <note>original: *matkala*</note>. It does not change and will not be changed, as it is written:
> **I am the Lord, I change not.** <note>Malachi 3:6</note>

**Rabbi Yehuda** said: All of them are shining cups, hanging from one another, and their foundation is that everything is one and not to be separated. And whoever separates them by his own power is separated from the Life of Worlds. **Rabbi Isaac** said: It is written:
> **And I will give children to be their princes, and babes shall rule over them.** <note>Isaiah 3:4</note>

This is what is written: "And the faces of the <term>Keruvim</term> <gloss>Cherubim</gloss>," and it is written: "He who sits upon the Cherubim," and it is written: "And He rode upon a Cherub and did fly." "He who sits upon the Cherubim" refers to when He begins to dwell in support; it is written "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>this is when He is found in perfection</note>. "And He rode upon a Cherub" <note>singular</note> refers to when the King does not dwell upon His throne. "He who sits upon the Cherubim" <note>plural</note> refers to two. Woe to the world when one Cherub turns its face away from its companion, for it is written:
> **And their faces shall look one to another.** <note>Exodus 26:20</note>

This is when there is peace in the world. **Rabbi Isaac** said: We have learned, "The nakedness of your daughter-in-law and the daughters of your father-in-law you shall not uncover." Woe to him who uncovers their nakedness. In this manner it is written of Jacob: "passing from end to end." And thus the portion of Israel with the Holy One, blessed be He, is found in their adornments, in the manner of that which is above, as it is written:
> **Israel, in whom I will be glorified.** <note>Isaiah 49:3</note>

Come and see, **Rabbi Isaac** said: In former days, when one said to his companion, "Show me one vessel and take money for it." Now a man says to his companion, "Take money and show me another," and there is no one to taste and no one to incline his portion, except for those few who are gathered and elevated to the Holy One, blessed be He. As it is written:
> **Thy people also shall be all righteous: they shall inherit the land for ever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.** <note>Isaiah 60:21</note>

Woe that the money is filled and sustained. **Rabbi Isaac** said: Woe, for I see those who are circumcised, all those who are crowned and stand above, searching. Woe that it is filled, and all those below hang upon them, woe. A window is opened for us, opened and polished and prepared from the smoke to the order that is upon them. And as in the Book of Concealment <note>original: *Sifra Detzniuta*</note> it is proven: woe above, woe below, and all of them rise in one balance. What is the "Concealment of the Book"? **Rabbi Hezekiah said:** These are the chapters that are all in the Great Palace and fill all the earth. **Rabbi Yehuda** said: All of them are superior in this way. **Rabbi [Abba] said:** Woe to him who deviates and bows, and to him who does not ascend and bow to them in this way.

### The Parable of the Wheat

A parable of a man who lived among the fields and did not know the dwellers of the city. He sowed wheat and ate the wheat in its raw form <note>as kernels</note>. One day he entered the city, and they brought him a good loaf of bread. He said, "What is this man-made thing for?" They said, "It is bread to eat." He ate and found it very pleasant to his taste. **He said,** "From what is this made?" They said, "Wheat." Later they brought him cakes kneaded in oil. He tasted them and said, "And what are these made of?" They said, "Wheat." Later they brought him royal pastries <note>original: *tariki*</note> made with honey and oil. He said, "And what are these sweets made of?" They said, "Wheat." He said, "Surely I am the master of all these things, for I eat the essence of all these, which is wheat." And because of that...

<meta>continues from previous page: Like</meta> a section in which the Name **YHWH Elohim** <note>original: "יה'וה אלהים"; the combination of the Tetragrammaton and the Name of Judgment</note> is mentioned, these actions are performed through all the attributes that are completed by the Attribute of Judgment <note>Hebrew: *Middat Ha-Din*</note> and the Attribute of Mercy <note>Hebrew: *Middat Ha-Rachamim*</note>. You will find this in the creation of the first man, in his judgment, and in his expulsion, and in all those matters; you will find that they all came about through both the Attribute of Judgment and the Attribute of Mercy. Everything was done in complete perfection, with mercy and judgment each according to what was appropriate in a judgment of truth.

According to this principle, the Torah says: "The Rock, His work is perfect" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>. The explanation of the verse is as follows: "The Rock" <note>Hebrew: *Ha-Tzur*</note> who decrees judgment with strength does not act with cruelty; He does not decree judgment until His work is "perfect" <note>Hebrew: *Tamim*</note>, meaning the judgment He decreed was first deliberated upon by the two attributes, Loving-kindness <note>Hebrew: *Chesed*</note> and Judgment <note>Hebrew: *Din*</note>. This is the meaning of "His work is perfect." For the term "perfect" <term>Tamim</term> is the secret of two things; it is as if it said "twins" <term>Te'omim</term>, but out of respect for the two supernal things, it uses the term *Tamim*.

Below, the term *Te'omim* is used. Thus it says: "And they shall be coupled <term>Te'omim</term> below... they shall be coupled <term>Tamim</term> at the head" <note>Exodus 26:24</note>. Below they are called *Te'omim*, above they are called *Tamim*. This is because below they appear as two distinct things, a thing and its opposite, like an advocate and an accuser. But above, everything is a single intention; whether advocate or accuser, both have one purpose. There is no hatred or love there, and no favoritism, only true justice. Therefore it says "His work is perfect," for He consulted with both Judgment and Mercy and then decreed the sentence. This is the secret of "True Judgment."

As for the phrase "For all His ways are justice" <note>Deuteronomy 32:4</note>, the explanation is that everything is visible to every eye, as it says "For all His ways are justice." You already know that Justice <term>Mishpat</term> is comprised of both Judgment and Mercy. For Justice corresponds to Jacob, who is the Middle Pillar <note>the central axis of the Sefirotic tree</note> that balances between the two "tents," which are Abraham and Isaac. Abraham corresponds to Loving-kindness <term>Chesed</term>, Isaac corresponds to Judgment <term>Din</term>, and Jacob decides between them: "A perfect man, dwelling in tents" <note>Genesis 25:27</note>. Justice corresponds to Jacob, drawing from Loving-kindness on Abraham's side and from Judgment on Isaac's side. Thus it says: "You have executed justice and righteousness in Jacob" <note>Psalm 99:4</note>.

The prophet said: "O Lord, correct me, but with justice; not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing" <note>Jeremiah 10:24</note>. The explanation of the verse "Correct me, O Lord, but with justice" <note>Hebrew: *Ach Be-Mishpat*</note> is that the word "but" <term>Ach</term> implies a division, as if to say: with the half of the attribute of Justice that is Loving-kindness. For Justice is half Judgment and half Loving-kindness. Therefore he said "but with justice," and then said "not in Your anger, lest You bring me to nothing," revealing the secret of diminishing the half of Justice that comes from the side of Anger.

Therefore, Justice is dependent on Jacob, who is the "father" among the tribes. Having known the great pain of children, when the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees against them, Jacob seeks mercy and righteousness for them. The secret of "And the Lord of Hosts is exalted in justice" <note>Isaiah 5:16</note>—what is written after it? "And the Holy God is sanctified in righteousness." This means that when Justice is exalted, Judgment is put to rest, turning toward the attribute of **El** <note>the Name associated with Chesed</note>. This is the secret of "The Holy God is sanctified in righteousness." ### **Torah** Or <gloss>Torah is Light</gloss>: These commandments mentioned in this portion are divided into three parts, which are the three pillars upon which the world stands: Torah, Divine Service, and Acts of Loving-kindness. Torah is represented by the commands "Do not add" and "Do not subtract," which indicate the perfection of the Torah. This is as the philosophers have said: a thing that is perfectly complete cannot be said to be lacking or excessive. For if it were lacking, it would not be complete; and if it could accept an addition, it would mean it was not previously finished. Therefore, the definition of "complete" is that which has neither deficiency nor excess. It is known that the Torah is dependent on His Great Name, which is <term>Y-H-V-H</term>, as in "The Torah of the Lord is perfect" <note>Psalm 19:8</note>, as I have elaborated in my commentary on Tractate Shevuot in the chapter "Torah Or." And as it says in the Zohar on the verse "This is My name and this is My memorial" <note>Exodus 3:15</note>: the letters <term>Y-H</term> with "My name" <note>Hebrew: Shemi</note> equals 365 <note>The number of negative commandments</note>; the letters <term>V-H</term> with "My memorial" <note>Hebrew: Zichri</note> equals 248 <note>The number of positive commandments</note>. It is written, "I am the first and I am the last" <note>Isaiah 44:6</note>; He is the absolute perfection, without subtraction or addition. Regarding this comes the warning, "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" <note>Deuteronomy 12:4</note>, which is a warning against erasing the Name or breaking a stone from the Holy Temple. Behold, the letters of the Name are the "house" in which He, blessed be He, dwells, as is the Temple. It is written, "I am the Lord, that is My name" <note>Isaiah 42:8</note>; the letters are like a frame for the house, and His Name, blessed be He, is the soul within them. One who destroys His house, as it were, destroys Him. This is the secret of "You shall not do so to the Lord your God." Service <note>Hebrew: Avodah</note> comprises most of the commandments mentioned in this portion. The command came to have a fixed place in the Chosen House, and the verse gives the reason: "To His habitation shall you seek, and there you shall come" <note>Deuteronomy 12:5</note>. "To His habitation" hints at the <term>Shekhinah</term> <gloss>Divine Presence</gloss>, which is the palace of the Name <term>Y-H-V-H</term>. Do not fear that she dwells there, for in the Temple, the Glory <note>Tiferet</note> is unified with His people. This is "to place His name there," which the Targum translates as "to cause His Presence to dwell." And "around the place of holiness the wicked walk," referring to the <term>Kelipot</term> <gloss>husks/forces of impurity</gloss>; therefore, "Take heed to yourself lest you offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see" <note>Deuteronomy 12:13</note>.

### **Sometimes** sparks of holiness spread outward, and it is a commandment to return them and bring them inside. This is the secret of the commandment to bring the firstborn offerings from outside the city to the Chosen House. Then the branch returns to its root, and it is written of them, "There you shall offer" <note>Deuteronomy 12:14</note>, meaning there they shall have an ascent <note>Hebrew: Aliyah</note> and not outside. Since the holiness is in the Chosen House, which is in the Holy Land, we are commanded to "turn away from evil" by destroying all the places where the nations worshipped. One must uproot and eradicate them, and this was commanded specifically in the Holy Land. The secret of this hints that the seventy nations, in their essence, are not idolaters <note>in the same way</note>; however, the nations in the Land of Israel, who are under the direct rule of the Honorable Name, worship by "cutting the plantings" <note>a metaphor for heresy</note>, and this is actual idolatry. Whereas outside the Land, they are under the rule of external forces. Just as there is a great prohibition against breaking a single stone of holiness, so conversely, it is a great commandment to destroy and eliminate a "Subverted City" <note>Ir HaNidachat</note> and never to rebuild it, for its place is impure. Likewise, one who entices or misleads <note>Meisit u-Madiach</note> must be uprooted, for he stems from the impurity of the Ancient Serpent who was an enticer. The Holy One immediately said, "Cursed is the serpent," therefore the powers of <term>Samael</term> <note>the angel of evil</note> are never pardoned. The command came not to love him and not to listen to him, as was said of the serpent: "I will put enmity between you and the woman" <note>Genesis 3:15</note>. A false prophet is also like an enticer. Let us return to the matter: the root of holiness is the Chosen House and Jerusalem. This is the reason for the first-fruits <note>Bikkurim</note>, which the priests have no permission to eat until they are placed in the Chosen House. For the first-fruits, being the "beginning," indicate great holiness; therefore, they go to the holy place, and from there they take their wisdom, for they are holy to God, and they eat in Jerusalem. The secret of "Lesser Holies" and the "Second Tithe" is that they are eaten in Jerusalem; this is the blessing of "grain, wine, and oil," which are the primary ancestors of all sustenance. It is forbidden to eat Lesser Holies until after the sprinkling of their blood, for the blood is the soul, and only afterward is there permission to enjoy the meat. Know that just as the Service—the sacrifice—is an offering to the Lord, so too is the worshiper. For the essence of the service is that one sacrifices himself, in the secret of "When a man <note>Adam</note> brings an offering from among you" <note>Leviticus 1:2</note>. The burnt offering <note>Olah</note> is entirely consumed because it comes to atone for the thoughts of the heart, which are spiritual; it is burned all night so the serpent cannot hinder it. Lesser Holies represent the peace of the soul and the body.

### **The secret** of the firstborn is the secret of "Holy Israel," who are called "Israel My firstborn" <note>Exodus 4:22</note>. He has pity on them and guards them, and they are called "the sheep of My pasture." Therefore, the firstborn animal is eaten only by priests. The secret of eating consecrated items corresponds to those with blemishes... for Holy Israel are called "Man" <note>Adam</note>. He was holy, but then a blemish fell upon him after he sinned and was clothed in "garments of skin," but he has a redemption through the secret of "I give a man in your stead." This was the secret of the <term>Azazel</term> goat which "bore their iniquities" <note>Leviticus 16:22</note>; their iniquities fall upon the head of the goat and its people. But we are commanded not to cause a blemish in a consecrated animal in order to eat it. For if one intentionally blemishes the holy, he damages the sanctity. There is also a prohibition against working or shearing consecrated animals, for even the "broken tablets" <note>of the Ten Commandments</note> remain holy.

### **The general principle** is that the Service is the sacrifice, but the internal sacrifice is the person himself. Likewise, his soul is called to the "Altar Above" after death, and Michael is the High Priest. This is the secret, for "in the image of God was man made." Therefore, the warning comes to be careful during his life regarding damages to souls, not to kill a person except after thorough inquiry and investigation. Then, he is "slain by the hand of Heaven," in the secret of "He is the witness, He is the judge," for the Lord is a true witness and a true judge. So must the Sanhedrin be; just as they are judges of truth, they must have witnesses of truth. I mean they must clarify the truth of the witnesses with complete clarity—inquiry and investigation—and then their judgment is like the judgment of Heaven. "Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones" <note>Psalm 116:15</note>.

### **Since** the death of His pious ones is precious—for Israel are holy from the side of their souls, and after death their souls cleave above—therefore the command comes: "You shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness..." <note>Deuteronomy 14:1</note> "for you are children to the Lord your God." This is not the case for the nations; cutting and baldness are their customs, as is fitting for them, since at death they go to destruction and have no portion in this world or the World to Come. We, however, are children of God. When we depart from this world, which is a temporary dwelling, we instead have a permanent residence above with our Father in Heaven. Therefore, it is forbidden to mourn excessively or perform these acts.

### **Let us return** to the matter: the person who worships is himself the sacrifice, as it says, "When a man brings an offering from among you." There is a further secret here: for a soul can be reincarnated even into a lower form, in the secret of "Man and beast You save, O Lord" <note>Psalm 36:7</note>. Therefore, even in eating non-consecrated meat <note>Chullin</note>, we are commanded regarding ritual slaughter <note>Shechitah</note> and great care that there be no nick in the blade, for then it becomes a carcass <note>Nevelah</note>, and "a disgrace <note>Nevalah</note> is committed in Israel." For who knows what reincarnation is within it? "Love your neighbor as yourself" <note>Leviticus 19:18</note>—choose for him a "beautiful death," meaning slaughter without a nick. If the animal dies on its own, the power of impurity takes hold of it. But when one slaughters it properly, and there is a spark of holiness in the animal or pure bird, then its soul departs in purity.

### **One who eats** a limb from a living animal is like one who eats the flesh of his own brother when a reincarnated soul is present. This is the secret of "You shall not eat the soul with the flesh" <note>Deuteronomy 12:23</note>. Likewise, the prohibition of forbidden foods and the signs of pure animals, beasts, and birds all indicate the spark spread within them—whether it is from the "Side of Impurity" or the "Side of Holiness." I have elaborated on this in Parashat Shemini. When Israel conducts itself with holiness, it is written of them, "And they shall make for Me a sanctuary, and I will dwell within them" <note>Exodus 25:8</note>. For they themselves are the Tabernacle, as man is divided into three parts: the head corresponds to the Holy of Holies; the heart corresponds to the Holy Place; and from the belly downward corresponds to the Courtyard, as I elaborated in Parashat Terumah. When one eats foods from the side of holiness, they are like sacrifices offered upon the Altar. Regarding this, our Sages said: "Now, a man's table atones for him," as I have explained elsewhere.

### **Regarding** the commandments of the Festivals and their sacrifices, I have written about each in its specific place. The command came to rejoice on the festivals and to go up for the pilgrimage: "Three times a year all your males shall appear." Do not read it only as "shall appear" <note>Hebrew: Yera'eh</note> but also "shall see" <note>Hebrew: Yir'eh</note>; just as one comes to see, he comes to be seen. Therefore, if one wishes to be seen in the Temple where the Glory dwells, he must "turn from evil and do good" and be a faithful servant to his Creator. Otherwise, it is forbidden for a wicked person to enter the hall; how could he wish to be seen before Him and bring a burnt offering of appearance? Then he himself becomes a sacrifice through the sacrifice he offers. It says "Three times a year he shall appear"—Isaac, who was a "perfect burnt offering"...

### On the shame sought from unworthy praises.
## DIALOGUE XXVI.

> Praise sparingly, for when you praise unjustly,
> If you later condemn, it will be a sign of levity.

*Sorrow.* I am accused of having praised an unworthy man.
<note>A large ornamental initial L begins the response of Reason.</note>
*Reason.* I am accused of having praised an unworthy man. Indeed, an evil thing often arises from a good root. For the good and innocent imagine others to be such as they are themselves. Hence they are even more prone to praising than is fair; and although I may admit it is bad to praise the unworthy, to disparage the undeserving is much worse.

*Sorrow.* I praised an unworthy man.

*Reason.* If you did so knowingly, you are blameworthy; but if unknowingly, you are excusable. It is a lesser evil to be deceived than to deceive. For to be deceived is the fault of another; but to deceive is the specific crime of the deceiver.

*Sorrow.* The praise of another turns into my infamy.

*Reason.* Rather, it is either your fault or your ignorance. For from another person, just as there is no true praise, so there is no infamy.

*Sorrow.* I grieve greatly for having praised an unworthy man.

*Reason.* See to it then that you do not often grieve for that very thing. Beware lest you leap forward rashly to praise or to disparage. Someone will eventually demonstrate in which parts of the heavens comets wander, why they travel so far removed from the rest, and how great or of what kind they are. Let us be content with what has been discovered; let posterity also contribute something to the truth. 

One says, "We do not see the things beyond through the stars, but we transmit our sight through comets." First, if that happens, it does not happen in that part where the star itself consists of thick and solid fire, but where a thin splendor runs out and disperses into hair <note>the comet's tail</note>. You see through the gaps in the fires, not through the fires themselves. 

"All stars," he says, "are round; comets are elongated, from which it appears they are not stars." But who will grant you that comets are long, when their nature is indeed a globe like the others? However, their brightness is extended just as the sun sends its rays far and wide. Yet the form of the sun itself is one thing, and the form of the light flowing from it is another. Thus the body of comets itself is rounded, but their splendor appears longer than that of other stars. 

"Why?" you ask. Tell me first why the moon receives a light so unlike the sun, though it receives it from the sun? Why is it sometimes red, sometimes pale? Why does it have a livid and black color when it is excluded from the sight of the sun? Tell me why all stars have a face somewhat unlike each other, and most different from the sun. Just as nothing prevents them from being stars even though they are not similar, so nothing prevents comets from being eternal and of the same condition as the rest, even if they do not have a similar face. 

Furthermore, if you consider the world itself, is it not composed of diverse things? Why is it that the sun always burns in Leo and parches the earth with heat, but in Aquarius it binds the winter and closes the rivers with frost? Yet both this star and that are of the same condition <margin>† it rises</margin>, though they are dissimilar in effect and nature. Aries is passed through <note>original: excolitur</note> in a very short time, Libra sinks most slowly, and yet both this star and that are of the same nature, though the former ascends in a brief time and the latter is brought forth for a long duration. Do you not see how contrary the elements are to each other? There are heavy and light things, cold and hot, moist and dry. The entire harmony of this world consists of discord. 

You deny that a comet is a star because its form does not correspond to the pattern, nor is it similar to the others. For you see, that star which returns to its place in the thirtieth year <note>Saturn</note> is very similar to this one which revisits its seat within a year. Nature does not perform its work according to a single form, but boasts in its very variety. It made some things slower, others swifter than the rest. Some it made stronger, others more temperate; some it led out from the crowd so they might proceed as single and conspicuous things, while others it sent into a flock. He is ignorant of nature's power who thinks she is never permitted to do anything except what she does most often. 

She does not show comets frequently; she assigned them another place, other times, and motions unlike the rest. She wished to honor the magnitude of her work through these things, whose face is too beautiful for you to think them accidental, whether you consider their size or their brightness, which is greater and more burning than the others. Indeed, their appearance has something remarkable and singular, not cast into a narrow space and squeezed, but let down more freely and embracing the region of many stars. 

Aristotle says that comets signify storms and the intemperance of winds and rains. What then? Do you not judge that to be a star which announces future events? For this is not a sign of a storm in the same way that oil sparking or rotting fungi forming are signs of future rain, or as it is an indication of a raging sea if sea-coots <term>Fulicæ</term> play on dry land, and leave their known marshes, and the heron <term>ardea</term> flies above the high cloud. <term>Phlebotomy</term> <gloss>bloodletting</gloss> is the evacuation specific to the blood when it is in equilibrium. As for evacuation specific to a humor that is excessive in quantity or corrupt in quality, it is not achieved through phlebotomy. Every excessive evacuation usually causes vomiting. If the cessation of a habitual diarrhea causes an illness, the remedy is usually to restore that evacuation; for example, if the cessation of a nosebleed or nasal discharge causes blockages, its return will remove them.

Know that the remaining matter which needs evacuation is less receptive to total extraction; pursuing it until the strength fails is dangerous. Often, the <term>nature</term> dissolves that remainder on its own. As long as the humor is of the type that should be expelled and the patient can bear it, do not fear excess. Sometimes you may even need to evacuate until fainting occurs. If a person has strong vigor but a large amount of bad humors, evacuate them little by little. Likewise, if the matter is highly matured or heavily mixed with the blood, it cannot be evacuated all at once, as is the case in sciatica, chronic joint pains, cancer, chronic scabies, and chronic boils.

Know that diarrhea draws from above and uproots from below, so it is suitable for the customary drawing of humors and also suitable after the materials have settled. If the materials are below, drawing them to the opposite direction <note>upward</note> and uprooting them from where they are is achieved by the act of drawing, and vice versa. The state of phlebotomy differs according to the sites from which the blood is taken, as you have learned. Those who least need evacuation are those with good digestion, and inhabitants of hot countries have little need for evacuation.

### Section Four: On Common Rules for Vomiting and Diarrhea and an Indication of How to Attract Purgative Medicine and Vomiting

We say: it is recommended for one who wishes to take a laxative to reduce or divide their food intake for a period, and first determine the amount they will test in a day in stages, making the foods and drinks varied. In this state, the stomach will desire to push what is in it upward or downward. As for uniform food, the stomach becomes satiated by it, grows heavy, and grips it tightly, especially if the quantity is small. For those with naturally soft bowels, none of this is necessary.

Know that the need for vomiting, diarrhea, and the like does not occur in those who follow a good <term>regimen</term> <gloss>lifestyle and diet</gloss>; they require what is lighter, and perhaps exercise, massage, and cupping will suffice for them. If the body becomes overfilled with the best of humors—namely blood—then phlebotomy is what is needed for purification, rather than diarrhea. If necessity dictates phlebotomy or evacuation in the autumn, begin with vomiting and delay phlebotomy; this is among the counsels of Hippocrates and the writings of Abylla, and it is the truth. Likewise, if phlegmatic humors are mixed with the blood. However, if the humors are equal but viscous and cold, phlebotomy may increase their thickness and viscosity; in such a case, one must begin with diarrhea.

In general, if the humors are equal, perform phlebotomy first, and if an excess remains, evacuate it. If they are unequal, evacuate the excess first until they are equal, then perform phlebotomy. Whoever prioritizes medicine over phlebotomy should have performed phlebotomy a few days prior. If someone has recently undergone phlebotomy and needs evacuation, drinking medicine will be more effective for them. Often, drinking medicine when phlebotomy was actually required results in vomiting and distress. If it does not settle with sedatives, then phlebotomy should have preceded it.

Not every evacuation is required due to excessive fullness; sometimes the severity of the illness or the fullness in quality and quantity demands it. Often, a good regimen makes the required phlebotomy unnecessary at the time. Frequently, a cause calls for evacuation but an obstacle arises, in which case the only trick is fasting, sleep, and correcting the <term>dyscrasia</term> <gloss>imbalance of temperament</gloss> caused by the fullness.

Some evacuations are for the sake of precaution, such as what is needed by those prone to gout or epilepsy at a known time, especially in spring; they need to take precautions before the time and undergo the specific evacuation, whether phlebotomy or diarrhea. Sometimes the use of external drying agents and desiccating medicines acts as an evacuation, as is done for those with dropsy. You may need to use a medicine that matches the humor to be evacuated in quality, such as <term>scammony</term> when you need to evacuate yellow bile; in that case, you must mix it with something that opposes it in quality but agrees with it in purging, such as <term>myrobalan</term>.

If a <term>dyscrasia</term> occurs afterward in those with inflammation of the viscera, their purging becomes weak. If forced to do so, use for them things like bindweed and safflower. As for laxatives and <term>cassia fistula</term>, Hippocrates said: "He whose upper parts are easy to respond to nature's call to vomit, the first step in his purification is to use vomiting in summer or spring." This protects the body from exhaustion. Know that one who is accustomed to drinking or has naturally loose bowels, or is not accustomed to vomiting in summer, should avoid it unless necessary.

One must prepare before diarrhea and vomiting by thinning the humor intended for evacuation and widening the passages. Know that for one who is emaciated in the abdominal walls, diarrhea and vomiting are difficult and exhausting. An emetic medicine may turn into a laxative if the stomach is strong, if taken during extreme hunger, if the drinker has loose bowels, or if the medicine is of a heavy substance that descends quickly. Conversely, a laxative may become an emetic due to weakness of the stomach, extreme heaviness, the medicine being repulsive, or the person having indigestion.

Every purgative medicine, if it does not purge due to lack of maturation, will stir the humor it was meant to purge and spread it through the body, overcoming the body and drawing other humors to it, thus increasing that humor in the body. Some humors respond more quickly to vomiting, such as yellow bile; others are resistant to vomiting, such as black bile. Some have a specific state, like <term>hellebore</term>, where its purging is more correct in itself. For those whose humor is descending, such as those with <term>slippery intestines</term> <gloss>chronic diarrhea</gloss>, the intestines grip, and purgative medicines composed of highly different ingredients during the time of purging become difficult, causing distress where the first part purges before the second, or the first part purges the second itself.

Whoever undergoes diarrhea while their body is clean will inevitably suffer from pain, colic, and distress, and the evacuation will be very difficult. In general, when medicine evacuates waste, there is no distress; if it is taken with distress, it is either evacuating something other than waste, or the humor being evacuated has changed. If the humor evacuated by vomiting or diarrhea changes to another humor, it indicates the body has been cleared of the intended humor.

They descend into the status of impurity through thought, but they do not ascend <note>meaning: lose their status of impurity</note> except through a physical action. An action removes an item from the status of both a previous action and a previous thought, but a thought does not remove an item from the status of either an action or a thought. And if we say that they are for the purpose of eating, they are made <note>susceptible</note> through thought and removed through thought. But did we not learn in a Mishnah: * All handles of food <term>yodot ha-okhalin</term> <gloss>parts of the food used for grasping</gloss> that are in the <term>siman</term> <gloss>stack/bundle</gloss> in the threshing floor are pure <note>not susceptible to impurity</note>, and Rabbi Yose deems them impure. It is well according to the one who says <term>siman</term> means they are bundled together, but according to the one who says what is <term>siman</term>? It means literally the herb <term>siman</term>, what is there to say? Here too, it refers to the actual herb. If so, what is the reason of the Rabbis? For they say like Rabbi Yose, as we learned: * Rabbi Yose deems them impure. This is well there, for the reason of Rabbi Yose is according to Rabbi Simeon ben Lakish, for Rabbi Simeon ben Lakish said: Since they are fit to be turned over with a pitchfork <term>atar</term>. But here, what are they fit for? One could say for catching the grain in their husks. The text itself states: All handles of food in the stack in the threshing floor are pure, and Rabbi Yose <note>deems them impure</note>. Simeon ben Lakish asked: What is <term>siman</term>? Rabbi Yochanan said: It is the actual herb. Rabbi Eleazar says: It refers to the binding of the stack. According to Rabbi Eleazar who said it is the actual herb, that is why Rabbi Yose deems it impure. But according to Rabbi Eleazar, why is the prayer of the righteous compared to a pitchfork <term>atar</term>? To tell you: just as this pitchfork turns the grain in the threshing floor from place to place, so too the prayer of the righteous turns the mind of the Holy One, Blessed be He, from the attribute of cruelty to the attribute of mercy.

### Question

The third article: whether more universal things are prior in our intellectual cognition.

Regarding the third, the procedure is as follows. It seems that more universal things are not prior in our intellectual cognition: because those things which are prior and better known according to nature are posterior and less known according to us; but universals are prior according to the nature of our intellect. Furthermore, composite things are prior to us compared to simple things, but universals are simpler, therefore they are known later by us. Furthermore, the Philosopher <note>Aristotle</note> says in the first book of the Physics that the defined thing first falls into our cognition, and the parts of the definition are less universal: just as "animal" is a part of the definition of "man," and universals are known later by us. Furthermore, we arrive at effects by chance and principles, but universals are known later by us. But on the contrary is what is said in the first book of the Physics, that we must proceed from universals to singulars.

I respond that it must be said that in the cognition of our intellect, two things must be considered. First, indeed, that intellectual cognition in some way takes its beginning from sensitive cognition; and because the sense is of singulars and the intellect is of universals, it is necessary that the cognition of singulars as far as we are concerned be prior to the cognition of universals. Second, it must be considered that our intellect proceeds from potentiality to act. And that which proceeds from potentiality to act first reaches an incomplete act, which is the middle between potentiality and act, and then a perfect act. The perfect act to which the intellect arrives is complete science, through which things are known distinctly and determinately; the incomplete act is imperfect science, through which things are known indistinctly under a certain confusion. For what is known in this way is known both in act and in a certain way in potentiality. As is said in the first book of the Physics: things that are more confused are first manifest and certain to us. Later, however, we know by distinguishing the principles and elements distinctly. It is manifest, moreover, that to know something in which many things are contained, without having proper knowledge of each of those things contained in it, is to know something under a certain confusion. In this way, both a whole in which parts are contained in potentiality and an integral whole can be known; for each whole can be known in a certain confusion without the parts being distinctly known. To know distinctly that which is contained in the whole is to have cognition of a less common thing: just as to know "animal" indistinctly is to know "animal" in which there is either "rational" or "irrational," which is to know "man" or "lion." Therefore, it first occurs to our intellect to know "animal" before knowing "man." And the same reasoning holds if we compare any more universal thing to a less universal one. As the sense goes out from potentiality into act, so does the intellect: and this order

<column-break/>

of cognition appears in the sense. For we judge more by sense when a thing is less known at a distance, perceiving it to be a body; and then perceiving it to be an animal; and then perceiving it to be a man; and finally perceiving it to be Socrates. Or it is pleasing and evident that a child from the beginning first distinguishes a man from a non-man; and children from the beginning call all men "fathers." Later, however, they determine each one specifically, as is said in the first book of the Physics. Thus, it is manifest that to know something indistinctly is still in potentiality, whether one knows the genus or the principle; and thus one knows the genus before one can know the differences. And so, in itself, indistinct cognition is the middle between potentiality and act. And that the cognition of singulars is prior as far as we are concerned, and the cognition of universals is prior in sensitive cognition and intellectual cognition. If both sense and intellect are considered, the more universal cognition is prior to the less universal and common.

To the first, it must be said that it can be considered in a twofold way. In one way, as it is considered according to the intention of truth. And since the intention of truth is true and the same, it has a relationship to many things. This comes about through the abstraction of the intellect as an end in this way, while truly it is posterior. In the first book On the Soul <note>Aristotle, De Anima</note>, it is said that the universal is either nothing or it is posterior; but Plato placed universals as substances; and in this consideration it is true, because particulars are nothing except through participation in the more universal subsisting things which are called Ideas. In another way, it can be considered regarding the nature itself of "animality" or "humanity" as it is found in particulars. And thus there is a twofold order of nature. One according to the way of generation and time, since in that way those things which are imperfect and in potentiality are prior. And in this way the more universal is prior in nature, which appears manifestly in the generation of man and animal. For first an animal is generated before a man, as is said in the book On the Generation of Animals. The other is the order of perfection or the intention of nature, just as act is simply prior in nature, and that which is perfect is prior to that which is imperfect; and in this way the less universal is prior in nature, as "man" is prior to "animal." For the intention of nature does not stop at the generation of an animal, but intends to generate a man.

To the second, it must be said that the more universal is compared to the less universal as a whole, because the whole contains the parts in potentiality. The more universal contains not only "man" and "horse," but also others. Thus, "animal" considered in itself is prior in our cognition to "man." If "man" were prior in our cognition to "animal," it would be through his specific reasoning.

To the third, it must be said that something can be known in two ways. In one way absolutely, according to what it is in itself, and thus nothing is known. In another way, as they are parts of this whole, like stones in a house; it is necessary that we first know the whole before the parts. For we first know the house in a certain confused way. Thus, it must be said that the defining terms, considered absolutely, are prior to us than the defined thing. Otherwise, the defined thing would not be made known through them. But they are more like parts.

He aligns this with the Aristotelian principle that the human intellect proceeds from potentiality to actual, perfected knowledge.</summary>
